assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy link a clear physiological discovery (the incretin effect, glucose-dependent insulin secretion, appetite and gastric effects) to drugs that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care and show broader cardiometabolic benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of patient impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion/actions), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide biology and therapeutic translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 form and its insulinotropic activity) form a plausible three-person configuration. Knudsen's pharmaceutical development of long-acting analogues is important but sits on the industrial side, and other early contributors (for example Habener) are not among the credited names, so allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed over decades with large independent randomized outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably pressing given the current clinical impact.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over who first defined the active peptide and its therapeutic use.
Whether the prize should reward physiology, peptide chemistry or drug development, and how to treat industrial contributors given the three-laureate limit.
Long-term safety and durability of the weight-loss and wider benefits are still accruing (my assessment, not independently verified).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as a dominant driver of synovial inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis and the clinical proof that TNF blockade works established the cytokine-targeted paradigm for chronic inflammatory disease. It changed outcomes across rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthropathies and opened biologic therapy as a class.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly carried the concept from human synovial cell cultures to controlled clinical trials, a clean two-person configuration. Contributions from TNF cloning and biology (for example Cerami, Old, Vilcek) and from antibody engineers are not in the supplied credit, so some allocation questions remain outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Decades of clinical use, multiple independent agents, and biosimilars confirm durability and the interpretation. Recognition is timely; the pioneers are elderly.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as a therapeutic application of a prior cytokine discovery rather than a fundamental discovery.
Credit for TNF biology and antibody engineering outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells expressing chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas and more recently in some autoimmune settings, a new modality of living drugs. The conceptual originality (receptor design with co-stimulation) and clinical impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation CAR design with co-stimulation, preclinical proof) and June (clinical translation, first durable responses) are central. Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials, and is a defensible third laureate, though he is arguably distinct from the CAR architecture itself. Eshhar and others are not in the credited list, which is a notable gap in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation; long-term follow-up now shows cures in a subset. Toxicity, solid-tumour limits and secondary malignancy signals mean the field is still evolving, but the core discovery is mature enough.
uncertainties: Omission of Zelig Eshhar and others from the supplied credit raises allocation issues.
Whether Rosenberg's TIL and adoptive-transfer work should be recognized as a separate contribution.
Limits in solid tumours and long-term safety.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cloning of the T-cell receptor solved the long-standing problem of how T cells recognize antigen with specificity and MHC restriction, and underpins nearly all modern cellular immunology, vaccine and immunotherapy concepts, including checkpoint and CAR-T approaches. Fundamental, original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Davis and Hedrick (mouse TCR beta chain via subtractive hybridization) and Mak (human TCR beta chain) were closely contemporaneous independent clonings; Yanagi's human clone is also credited, so a three-person prize forces an exclusion. I propose Davis, Hedrick and Mak with acknowledged uncertainty about Yanagi.
assessment.maturity: Established for four decades with total independent confirmation; the delay is a concern only in that it is overdue and some contributors may be elderly or deceased (not verified).
uncertainties: Exclusion of Yanagi under the three-laureate limit.
Whether the committee will consider this too old relative to later therapeutic advances, and living status of the contributors is not verified by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition created the template for molecularly targeted cancer therapy, converting chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a chronically managed one with near-normal life expectancy. Clear, original translational impact with proof of principle for oncogene addiction.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery programme and kinase inhibitor chemistry), Druker (preclinical demonstration of selective CML inhibition and the clinical trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation drugs) cover a coherent chain. Chemistry colleagues (for example Zimmermann) and the Rowley/Nowell/Hungerford discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and Baltimore/Witte on BCR-ABL precede it and are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of survival data, extensive independent confirmation and resistance understanding; recognition is mature and long overdue.
uncertainties: Pharmaceutical team credit and the role of earlier cytogenetic and oncogene discoveries.
Whether this is recognised as drug development rather than discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV prevent persistent infection and cervical, anogenital and oropharyngeal precancers and cancers, with population-level reductions in cervical disease now documented. A rare case of cancer prevention by vaccination with major global health impact.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (parallel VLP work and clinical translation) are the central contributors; Zhou (with Frazer) and others also had claims, and the 2008 prize for HPV's role in cervical cancer (zur Hausen) is separate. A three-person configuration is feasible but some credit disputes exist.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data from several countries and consistent independent trials; timely and mature.
uncertainties: Priority dispute among the groups that produced VLPs (including Jian Zhou's role) is not resolved in the supplied credit.
Possible concern that recognition of HPV science was partly delivered in 2008.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification and cloning of IL-6 (BSF-2), its receptor and gp130 signalling, and the development of tocilizumab, defined a central cytokine in autoimmune and inflammatory disease, cytokine release syndrome and beyond. High originality, with wide therapeutic uptake in rheumatoid arthritis, giant-cell arteritis and CAR-T toxicity.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano are the clear pair credited with cloning and characterisation of IL-6 and its receptor, a clean two-person configuration. Other groups cloned related factors independently (for example Content, Van Snick, Revel), which raises minor priority questions.
assessment.maturity: Decades of clinical use and extensive independent validation; mature and timely.
uncertainties: Independent discovery claims for IL-6 in the 1980s.
Whether the committee prefers TNF as the representative cytokine-targeting prize, making IL-6 secondary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defines how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, interferon induction, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies such as Aicardi-Goutieres), antiviral defence and anti-tumour immunity. It is a clear, original mechanistic discovery with strong links to autoimmune disease and therapeutic programmes.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP, which is the decisive mechanistic step; Barber discovered STING. Ishikawa, Sun and Wu are credited as contributors but are secondary on the available information, so a two-person prize seems fair.
assessment.maturity: Strongly replicated and widely extended, but clinical translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet delivered approved therapies; recognition may be a little early but not premature as a fundamental discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the lack of approved therapies makes this less mature than other candidates.
Roles of Ishikawa (who co-discovered STING with Barber's group era) and of cyclic dinucleotide pioneers (Vance, Hopfner, others) are not fully reflected in the credited names.
